title: Replace the charging port on a clip-back phone
tools: Tray or mat to keep screws in order
parts: Replacement charging board or flex made for your exact phone model

diyCheck.summary: This is a sample guide for learning the general method on a clip-back phone with a separate charging board. Your phone's layout may differ, so also check a guide written for your exact model.
goToShopIf: The charging port is soldered directly to the mainboard
The battery is swollen or the back is lifting by itself
The phone has been in water or has burn marks
You do not have a replacement part made for your exact model

steps.title: Check the port is really the problem
steps.body: Power the phone off. Try a charger and cable you know work. Shine a light into the port and gently remove any lint with a soft brush or a wooden toothpick. Many charging problems end here, with no need to open the phone.
warnings: Never put metal, such as a pin or needle, into the charging port.
checklist: Tried a charger and cable that work
Port is clean, and the fault is still there

steps.title: Prepare the phone and your workspace
steps.body: Back up your data. Keep the phone powered off and unplugged. Lay out your tray and anti-static mat, and clear the table of anything that can burn.
checklist: Wrist strap is on and grounded

steps.title: Remove the SIM tray and outer screws
steps.body: Take out the SIM tray and any visible screws. Check under stickers and rubber plugs for hidden screws. Keep everything in order on your tray.
checklist: Visible and hidden screws are removed and in order

steps.title: Release the clips
steps.body: Slide a plastic opening tool into the seam and work around the phone so the clips release one at a time. You will hear small clicks. If a section will not move, look for a screw you missed before using more force.
warnings: Keep the tool shallow, and never push it toward the battery.

steps.title: Disconnect the battery
steps.body: Remove any inner plate that covers the battery connector. Lift the connector straight up with a plastic spudger, then bend it slightly away from the socket so it cannot touch again.
warnings: Use plastic only. A metal tool can short the connector and cause sparks.
checklist: Connector cannot spring back onto the socket

diyGate.question: The phone is open and you are about to work near the battery. Look at it closely.
stopIf: The battery looks puffy, dented or punctured
You can see corrosion or signs of water inside
The phone feels hot while switched off

steps.title: Remove the lower cover
steps.body: Unscrew the plastic cover over the bottom of the phone and lift it off. It often holds the loudspeaker, so note how it sits before you move it.
checklist: Screws are laid out in order

steps.title: Remove the old charging board
steps.body: Take a photo so you can see how the thin antenna cable is routed. Unclip the antenna cable with the spudger, lifting straight up. Unplug the flex that links the charging board to the mainboard, remove any screws, and lift the board out.
warnings: The antenna cable connector is delicate. Do not pull on the wire.
checklist: Took a photo of the cable routing
Old board is out with no torn cables

diyGate.question: This guide only works if the port is on its own removable board.
stopIf: The port is soldered to the mainboard
The new part does not match the old one exactly

steps.title: Fit the new charging board
steps.body: Set the new board in place and refit its screws. Press the flex connector straight down until it clicks, then snap the antenna cable back on. Route the cable the way it looks in your photo.
checklist: Antenna cable is back on and routed correctly

steps.title: Reconnect the battery and test
steps.body: Refit the lower cover, then press the battery connector down until it clicks. Power on and test charging, a data connection to a computer, the microphone and mobile signal, before you close the phone.

steps.title: Close the phone
steps.body: Power the phone off. Line up the back cover and press around the edges until every clip snaps in. Refit the outer screws and the SIM tray, then do one last charging test.
warnings: If the cover will not close flat, stop and check for a pinched cable.
checklist: Cover sits flat all the way around
All screws are back in place
